source_name: RUSI — MONEYVAL mutual evaluation report summaries (incl. North Macedonia)
why_relevant: Condensed, comparable English summaries of the MONEYVAL findings — cheap triage layer before reading the full evaluation.

source_name: SeeNews — North Macedonia economy/banking wire
why_relevant: Regional SEE business wire with dense, dated English items on NBRNM policy-rate and reserve-requirement decisions, rating actions and bank news — fastest English tripwire on MK central-bank actions.

source_name: bne IntelliNews — North Macedonia country feed
why_relevant: Correspondent-based English coverage of MK banking, payments and fintech entrants (e.g. Nayax cashless rollout) plus regional AML/bank-failure investigations; useful for market-context around regulatory moves.

source_name: Central Banking — National Bank of North Macedonia organisation page
why_relevant: Specialist English trade press tracking NBRNM appointments, supervisory initiatives, fintech/CBDC-adjacent work and governor statements — a vendor-style monitor of central-bank behaviour.

source_name: BIS central bankers' speeches — NBRNM governor addresses
why_relevant: BIS archives English translations of NBRNM governor speeches (fintech strategy, digital payments, supervision priorities) — often the earliest English statement of a coming regulatory initiative, and a durable archive.

source_name: EBA — Opinion on CRR third-country equivalence for North Macedonia
why_relevant: EU-side technical assessment of whether MK supervisory and regulatory arrangements are equivalent to the CRR — a rare external benchmark of MK supervision quality with direct consequences for EU banks' MK exposures.

source_name: Fitch Ratings — North Macedonia sovereign and banking-sector commentary (incl. PDFs mirrored on Ministry of Finance portal)
why_relevant: Rating reports carry dated banking-sector metrics (capital, NPL, ROE) and commentary on supervisory and regulatory developments; the MK finance ministry mirrors the PDFs, giving open access to otherwise gated content.

source_name: MIA (Media Information Agency) — English service
why_relevant: State news agency English wire relaying Ministry of Finance and NBRNM announcements (rating affirmations, law adoptions) — an English-language bridge to MK-language official statements.

source_name: Western Balkans Info Hub — enlargement document mirror
why_relevant: Independent mirror of EU enlargement documents (hosts the 2025 North Macedonia report PDF) — an archival fallback when Commission URLs rotate.

source_name: US ITA — North Macedonia Country Commercial Guide (trade financing / banking chapter)
why_relevant: Annually refreshed English overview of the MK banking system, supervisory authority and payment practices, written for foreign entrants — a stable baseline reference and public-domain.

source_name: Multilaw Business Guides — North Macedonia: Payment services
why_relevant: Law-firm-network comparative business guide with a dedicated MK payment-services section; low-cost English cross-check on licensing categories and perimeter.

source_name: ЕСЈН — Електронски систем за јавни набавки (Electronic Public Procurement System)
why_relevant: Single mandatory national portal where every contracting authority (Ministry of Finance, Treasury, NBRSM, UJP, Customs, Health Fund, state-owned entities, municipalities) publishes annual procurement plans, contract notices (огласи), tender documentation, award decisions and realised contracts. Payment/card/ATM/POS/core-banking/compliance tenders in MK surface here first, usually with the regulatory driver and the delivery deadline stated in the tender documentation.

source_name: Биро за јавни набавки (Bureau for Public Procurement, BJN) — Огласи and institutional site
why_relevant: The BJN is the regulator/operator of the procurement system inside the Ministry of Finance. Its site carries the notices feed, the legal framework (Закон за јавните набавки), handbooks, an interactive open-data search platform over all institutions' procurement, and annual reports on the state of the procurement system — the best pointer layer for discovering contracting authorities and rule changes that shape how banking/payments tenders are framed.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Е-јавни набавки / Јавни набавки section
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance is both the policy owner for payments/financial-sector legislation and a major contracting authority (Treasury/Трезор systems, PFM reform IT, tax and customs adjacent systems). Its own procurement pages carry MoF-run tenders and mirror IFI-funded national-market notices.

source_name: CFCD — Central Financing and Contracting Department, Ministry of Finance (IPA contracting authority) — Tenders
why_relevant: Sole contracting authority for EU IPA-funded projects in North Macedonia — the channel through which donor-funded regulator/supervisor modernisation (PFM, tax, customs, financial supervision IT, AML/compliance systems) is tendered. Notices state the EU-accession-driven requirement and the implementation deadline.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU Official Journal supplement), North Macedonia notices
source_subtype: supranational tender gazette with open API
why_relevant: Above-threshold MK notices and EU/IPA-funded notices with North Macedonia as place of performance are published in TED. TED is fully machine-readable (search API + bulk XML/notice packages) and is the cleanest structured feed for cross-border payment/card/core-banking/compliance procurement touching MK.

source_name: EBRD Client eProcurement Portal (ECEPP) — North Macedonia notices
why_relevant: EBRD-financed projects in MK (municipal, energy, financial-institution and public-sector modernisation) tender through ECEPP; IFI notices capture donor-funded systems work that never appears on the national portal, and PIU/consultant notices signal projects 12-24 months before implementation tenders.

source_name: World Bank project procurement — P176366 'Building Effective, Transparent and Accountable PFM Institutions' (North Macedonia) procurement plans & STEP notices
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance-implemented PFM project explicitly covers Macro-Economy & Public Finance and ICT/Telecommunications; its published procurement plan enumerates forthcoming goods/consultancy packages (treasury, tax, PFM IT) with methods, estimated values and dates — an early-warning list of upcoming state financial-systems tenders. National-market packages are cross-published on ESJN and the MoF site.

source_name: Државна комисија за жалби по јавни набавки (State Appeals Commission for Public Procurement, DKZJN)
why_relevant: Publishes filed complaints daily and decisions from its sessions. Appeals against payment/card/ATM/core-banking tenders reveal specification disputes, which vendors bid, and whether award timelines (and therefore compliance deadlines) slip — information not visible in the notice itself.

source_name: Народна банка на Република Северна Македонија (NBRSM) — institutional site incl. procurement/legal documents
why_relevant: The central bank is the operator of the national payment systems (MIPS, KIBS oversight) and the supervisor. It is a contracting authority and hosts procurement-law and payment-system documents; its tenders for payment-system, cash-handling and supervisory-reporting systems are the most direct proxy for upcoming payments obligations.

source_name: Царинска управа (Customs Administration of North Macedonia) — Јавни набавки document store
why_relevant: Customs runs large, regulation-driven IT programmes (customs declaration processing system CDPS, new ICT system, EU-alignment-driven interfaces) and publishes full tender documentation as PDFs on its own site — a rich, parseable source of technical specifications and delivery deadlines for state financial-systems procurement adjacent to payments and compliance.

source_name: Управа за јавни приходи (Public Revenue Office, UJP) — fiscalisation regulation & procurement procedure
why_relevant: UJP owns fiscalisation (фискализација) rules that directly govern POS/fiscal-device and card-acceptance obligations for merchants, and is itself a contracting authority with a published procurement procedure. Its regulation index plus its tenders link the compliance obligation to the procurement that implements it.

source_name: Фонд за здравствено осигурување (Health Insurance Fund, FZO) — Јавни набавки and electronic health card
why_relevant: Large state-fund contracting authority; runs the national electronic health card (електронска здравствена картичка) programme — card issuance, personalisation, readers and supporting infrastructure. Directly relevant to card-technology demand and to Printec-type card/issuance business outside the banking sector.

source_name: Министерство за дигитална трансформација (Ministry of Digital Transformation) — Јавни набавки & Отворени податоци
why_relevant: Policy owner for digital identity, interoperability and open data — the horizontal layer that digital-payment and e-government payment tenders depend on. Its own procurement and its open-data agenda flag upcoming national digital infrastructure that payment vendors plug into.

source_name: Портал за отворени податоци — data.gov.mk (national open data portal, incl. procurement datasets)
why_relevant: Publishes machine-readable datasets from public institutions with an API for automated download/updating; procurement-as-open-data is an explicit Open Government Partnership commitment for MK. Best route to bulk, structured historical tender data without scraping ESJN's ASP.NET UI.
